newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut up after Banque Audi's s.
newsitem.headline: Beirut up after Banque Audi's s.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour Le Commerce rose 4.5 percent to $17.25 on Monday and brokers said a surge in Banque Audi 's price last week pushed the market up.
Brokers said Solidere A and B shares were an "interesting buy" at $10.25 and $11 respectively from $10.5 and $10.75.
Banque Audi, which traded at $23 before the weekend, fell to $22.5 in "temporary profit-taking". A block of 5,600 Audi shares traded on the BSE at $23 on Monday.
"BLC has risen because of Audi which has established a new benchmark on the market, pushing BLC up," a broker said.
Georges Abou Jaoude, Director of Lebanese operations at Beirut finance house Financial Funds Advisors said: "It is an arbitrage situation. I expect BLC to rise further amid heavy demand".
Demand for BLC on Monday was 85,995 shares against a supply of 12,350. Three blocks of BLC totalling 17,500 shares traded on the floor at prices ranging between $16.75 and $17.25.
Abou Jaoude told Reuters that Audi fell in "small and temporary profit-taking". Last week, the share rose 15 percent in three days.
Bank of Beirut, the third bank listed on the exchange, rose 1.75 percent to $3.625 from $3.5625.
"BOB has been stable around these price levels for sometime now. Its stability is building a momentum for possible rises following the announcement of the bank's second quarter results," he said.
The LIBX bank index rose 1.34 percent to 145.89. The BLOM general index fell 0.61 percent to 924.80 and the LISPI general index fell 0.27 percent to 88.30.

Abou Jaoude said Solidere shares were drawing increased interest because supply of A shares, distributed to former holders of property rights in Beirut's central district, was diminishing at a high rate.
"Also making the share attractive is the dividend yield over a one-year term," he added.
Shareholders in Solidere are expected to approve a 25 cents dividend during an upcoming general assembly while -- 25 percent up on the 1995 dividend.
Total BSE turnover was 246,796 shares from 146,000 and value was $2,696,513 from $1,682,000.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Eternit fell to $1.9375 from $2 while Ciments Blancs fell to $5 from $5.1875. Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.28125.
There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic shares.
